title: The Last Message
subtitle: A Romance Thriller — Season One
author: Salman Adan
description: Adam never believed in love at first sight. Then he met Ayan—the quiet girl in red who slowly became the most important person in his life. But their romance is built on secrets. When Ayan suddenly disappears after sending Adam a terrifying warning, he discovers that someone has been watching them from the beginning.

chapters.title: The Girl In Red
chapters.text:
Adam never believed in love at first sight. He believed in
conversations. In the little things people did when they thought
nobody was watching. The way someone smiled when they were
genuinely happy. The way they looked away when they were
hiding something. The silence between two people that somehow
felt more intimate than words. That was why he remembered the
girl in red. It was a warm Saturday afternoon in Nairobi when
Adam first saw her. He was standing outside a crowded training
hall, scrolling through his phone while everyone waited for the
next session to begin. Then he heard laughter. Not loud. Not
attention-seeking. Just genuine. He looked up. She was standing
with two friends near the entrance, wearing a simple red scarf.
She was laughing at something one of them had said, her eyes
narrowing slightly as her smile grew. Adam looked away. Then
looked back. He smiled to himself. "Don't stare." He tried. He
failed. For the rest of the afternoon, he kept noticing her. Not
because she was trying to be noticed. That was exactly what
caught his attention. She seemed comfortable being herself.
When the training ended, everyone began leaving. Adam walked
toward the bus. A few minutes later, she appeared. Same red
scarf. Earphones in her ears. Quiet. She took a seat near the
window. Adam sat several rows behind her. He didn't know her
name. He didn't know where she lived. He didn't even know if
he'd ever see her again. But somehow, he already knew one
thing. He wanted to. Three weeks later, they met again. This
time, she knew his name. "Adam, right?" He looked at her,
surprised. "You remember?" She smiled. "Maybe." "Maybe?" She
shrugged. "You're not that easy to forget." He laughed. That was
the beginning. Not a dramatic beginning. No music. No rain. No
impossible coincidence. Just two people talking. And sometimes,
the biggest stories begin quietly. Their conversations became
longer. Then later. Then every day. At first, they talked about
ordinary things. Music. Family. Food. Dreams. The stupid things
that made them laugh. But slowly, the conversations changed.
They started telling each other things they didn't tell everyone
else. Adam learned that Ayan hated being lied to. Ayan learned
that Adam could forgive almost anything except betrayal. They
learned each other's silences. And somewhere between the good

mornings and the good nights, Adam realized something
terrifying. He was falling for her. Not all at once. Quietly. Little
by little. The way night takes over a city without anyone noticing
exactly when daylight disappeared. One evening, they were
talking on the phone. "You know what I like about you?" Ayan
asked. "What?" "You're calm." Adam laughed. "That's because
you haven't seen me angry." "I don't want to." "You should be
careful." "Why?" "Because one day you might become the reason
I'm angry." There was silence. Then she laughed. "Never." Adam
smiled. He wanted to believe her. He really did. Two months
later, they were officially together. Adam thought that was when
their story truly began. He was wrong. Their story had begun
long before either of them realized. Because there was something
Ayan hadn't told him. Something from her past. Something that
had been waiting patiently for her to fall in love again. And
someone else had been waiting too. Watching. Listening.
Learning everything about them. Even their smallest
conversations. Even their private jokes. Even the way Adam said
goodnight. Someone knew. Someone was watching. And Adam
wouldn't discover the truth until it was already too late.

chapters.title: A Message At Midnight
chapters.text:
It was 12:17 a.m. Adam was half asleep when his phone
vibrated. One message. From Ayan. Ayan: Are you awake? Adam
smiled. Adam: For you? Always. The typing indicator appeared.
Disappeared. Appeared again. Then nothing. Adam waited. A
minute passed. Then another. Finally, her message arrived. Ayan:
I need to tell you something. Adam sat up. Adam: What
happened? No reply. He called. The phone rang. Once. Twice.
Three times. Then the call ended. He called again. This time, the
phone was switched off. A strange feeling settled in his chest.
Then his phone vibrated. A message. But this one was different.
There was no greeting. No emoji. No explanation. Just one
sentence. Ayan: If anything happens to me, don't trust the person
who tells you I left. Adam stared at the screen. He read it again.
And again. His heart began beating faster. Adam: What do you
mean? Delivered. No reply. Adam: Ayan? Delivered. Nothing.
Then, suddenly— The message disappeared. Adam froze. He
refreshed the conversation. Gone. The entire message was gone.
He called her again. Nothing. He opened their previous
conversation. Everything looked normal. Almost too normal. Then
he noticed something. A message from three days earlier. One he
didn't remember receiving. Unknown number: You should stop
asking questions. Adam stared at it. His hands became cold. He
didn't sleep that night. At 6:42 a.m., he called Ayan again. Her
phone was still off. At 7:15, he went to her house. She wasn't
there. Her mother looked confused when he asked for her. "She
left early yesterday," she said. "Yesterday?" "Yes." Adam's
stomach tightened. "Where did she go?" Her mother shook her
head. "She didn't say." Adam looked toward the road. Something
was wrong. Very wrong. Then his phone vibrated. Unknown
number. One message. Unknown: You were warned. Adam stared
at the screen. And for the first time, he understood. Ayan hadn't
disappeared. Someone had made her disappear. And somehow...
he was next.

chapters.title: She Wasn'T Supposed To Know
chapters.text:
SHE WASN'T SUPPOSED TO
KNOW
Adam spent the entire morning trying to convince himself that
he was overreacting. People disappeared for ordinary reasons.
Phones died. Plans changed. Messages got deleted. There had to
be an explanation. There had to be. But every explanation he
created collapsed under the same question: Why had someone
warned him? By noon, Adam was sitting alone in a small café
near the training center where he had first met Ayan. He hadn't
ordered anything. His phone lay on the table. The unknown
number hadn't messaged again. He opened his conversation with
Ayan. He scrolled through months of messages. There were
hundreds. Good mornings. Good nights. Arguments that lasted
ten minutes and apologies that lasted an hour. Pictures. Voice
notes. Inside jokes. Ayan had become part of his daily life so
naturally that he couldn't remember what his days looked like
before her. Then he noticed something. A photograph. It was one
Ayan had sent him nearly a month ago. She had taken it from
inside a car. At first, Adam had thought nothing of it. Now he
zoomed in. The photograph showed Ayan sitting by a window.
Behind her was a street. A petrol station. A blue building. And
reflected faintly in the window... a black Toyota. Adam's eyes
narrowed. He recognized it. He had seen the same car several
times. Near the training center. Near Ayan's house. Once outside
a restaurant where they had gone for dinner. He had always
assumed it belonged to someone nearby. Now he wasn't so sure.
Adam saved the photograph. Then his phone rang. "Hello?"
Silence. "Hello?" A man's voice finally answered. "You should stop
looking for her." Adam stood. "Who is this?" "You don't know
what you're getting yourself into." "Where is Ayan?" Another
silence. Then the man said something that made Adam's blood
run cold. "Ask her about the night in Garissa." The call ended.
Adam stared at the screen. Garissa. He knew that place. He
remembered the trip. The bus. The long road. Ayan sitting near
the window with her earphones in. That red scarf. He
remembered watching her without her knowing. Or at least... he
thought she hadn't known. That evening, Adam went to see the
one person who might know what was happening. Rayan. His

closest friend. They met at a quiet roadside café. Rayan listened
without interrupting. When Adam finished, Rayan leaned back.
"You're sure this isn't some prank?" "I'm sure." "Did the guy tell
you who he was?" "No." "And you still want to keep looking?"
Adam looked at him. "She's the woman I love." Rayan sighed. "I
know." For a moment, neither spoke. Then Rayan asked: "What
happened in Garissa?" Adam shook his head. "I don't know."
Rayan looked away. It was only for a second. But Adam noticed.
"What?" "Nothing." "Rayan." "I'm just saying... maybe you should
leave this alone." "Why?" "Because sometimes people have
secrets for a reason." Adam leaned forward. "You know
something." Rayan didn't answer. "Rayan." Finally, he looked at
Adam. "I've heard the name before." "What name?" "Ayan."
Adam's expression changed. "From where?" Rayan hesitated.
"Someone mentioned her a long time ago." "Who?" "I don't
remember." Adam stared at him. "You expect me to believe that?"
Rayan stood. "I'm trying to protect you." "From what?" Rayan
didn't answer. He simply walked away. That night, Adam went
through everything Ayan had ever told him about Garissa. He
remembered a conversation they had during the bus ride. She
had been unusually quiet that day. He had asked her: "What's
wrong?" "Nothing." "You've been quiet." "I'm just tired." He
remembered smiling at her. "You're lying." She had looked at
him. Then smiled. "You notice too much." At the time, he thought
she was teasing him. Now he wasn't sure. Adam searched his
phone again. There. A voice note. From that same night. He had
never listened to it. He pressed play. At first, there was only the
sound of wind and the bus engine. Then Ayan's voice. Soft.
Almost whispering. "If you're listening to this..." A pause. "...then
something went wrong." Adam froze. The recording continued. "I
don't know who I can trust anymore." Another pause. "I wanted
to tell you." Her voice cracked. "But I was afraid." Adam leaned
closer to the speaker. "There's something about me you don't
know." The recording suddenly became distorted. Then a man's
voice could be heard faintly in the background. "Ayan." She
stopped speaking. The recording ended. Adam immediately
played it again. Then again. His hands were shaking. Someone
had been on that bus with her. Someone she knew. Someone she
was afraid of. Adam checked the date. The voice note had been
recorded almost two months before they officially started dating.
Which meant Ayan had been hiding something from him from the
very beginning. At 2:03 a.m., Adam received another message.
This time, there was a photograph attached. He opened it. His
heart stopped. It was a picture of him and Ayan. They were

sitting together in the car. Ayan was smiling. Adam was looking
at her. Neither of them knew they were being photographed. The
picture had clearly been taken from a distance. Below it was one
sentence: She wasn't supposed to tell you. Adam stared at the
photograph. Then another message appeared. Unknown: Now
you know why she chose you. Adam's fingers tightened around
the phone. Adam: Who are you? Three dots appeared. Then
disappeared. Appeared again. Finally, a reply. Unknown: Ask
your friend why he was in Garissa that night. Adam stopped
breathing. Rayan. He immediately called him. No answer. He
called again. Still nothing. Then Adam noticed something else.
The photograph's metadata showed the picture had been taken
three days earlier. Someone had been following them recently.
Not months ago. Not weeks ago. Three days. While they were still
together. While Ayan was still smiling. While Adam thought they
were safe. He looked around his dark room. The curtains were
closed. The door was locked. But suddenly, the room didn't feel
private anymore. His phone vibrated. One final message.
Unknown: Don't trust Rayan. Adam stared at the words. Then— A
knock came from his front door. Three slow knocks. Adam didn't
move. Another three knocks. He reached for the nearest object he
could use as protection. Then his phone rang. It was Rayan. Adam
answered. For several seconds, neither of them spoke. Then
Rayan whispered: "Adam..." "Where are you?" "I'm sorry." Adam's
heart sank. "Sorry for what?" Rayan's voice trembled. "Because
Ayan was never the one they were looking for." A pause. "They
were looking for you." The line went dead.

chapters.title: The Night In Garissa
chapters.text:
Adam stood completely still. Rayan's last words kept repeating
in his head. They were looking for you. He called back. Once.
Twice. Nothing. He tried again. The phone was switched off.
Adam looked toward the door. The knocking had stopped. That
somehow frightened him more. He moved quietly toward the
window and pulled the curtain aside. The street outside was
almost empty. A streetlight flickered across the road. Nothing
unusual. Then he saw it. A black Toyota. Parked beneath a tree.
Engine running. Adam stepped away from the window. His phone
vibrated. A message from Rayan. Rayan: Don't leave your house.
Another message came immediately. Rayan: They're watching the
door. Adam's heart pounded. He turned off the lights. Then his
phone rang. Ayan. Adam stared at the screen. For a moment, he
couldn't breathe. Ayan is calling... He answered. "Ayan?" Silence.
"Ayan, where are you?" A faint breath came through the speaker.
Then her voice. Barely audible. "Adam..." He closed his eyes.
"Where are you?" "I can't tell you." "Are you hurt?" "No." "Then
please—tell me where you are." "I need you to listen to me." Her
voice trembled. "Don't trust Rayan." Adam froze. "You know
about him?" "Yes." "What happened?" "I found out too late."
"What?" She took a shaky breath. "The night in Garissa..." A loud
sound interrupted her. She gasped. "Someone's here." "Ayan?"
"Adam, listen to me." Her voice became urgent. "There's a reason
I chose you." "What reason?" Silence. Then she whispered: "Your
father." The call ended. Adam stood frozen. His father had been
dead for nine years. And Ayan had never met him. Adam sat on
the floor. His mind raced through memories. His father's old
photographs. His work. His friends. His death. Everything he
thought he knew suddenly felt incomplete. He remembered
something his father used to say when Adam was young. "Some
things are safer forgotten." At the time, Adam thought it was just
something adults said. Now it sounded like a warning. He opened
the old family photographs stored on his phone. One by one.
Nothing. Then he remembered an old wooden box his mother
kept in the house. He found it beneath her bed. Inside were
documents, photographs, letters and an old key. Adam picked up
a photograph. His father was standing beside three men. Adam
recognized one immediately. Rayan's father. His hands went cold.

He turned the photograph over. There was a date written on the
back. August 17, 2017 — Garissa. Adam stared at it. The same
place. The same year. The same mystery. Then he noticed
something else. Ayan's name was written on the back. Not her
full name. Just: A. Hassan Adam's breathing stopped. How could
his father have known her? A sound came from behind him. The
front door. Opening. Adam quickly switched off his phone screen.
Someone was inside. He heard footsteps. Slow. Careful. Coming
toward the room. Adam grabbed the old wooden box and moved
behind the bedroom door. The footsteps stopped. Silence. Then a
man's voice. "Adam?" He recognized it. Rayan. Adam stepped out.
"Why are you here?" Rayan looked exhausted. His shirt was
stained with blood. Adam immediately stepped back. "Whose
blood is that?" Rayan closed the door. "Not mine." "Where is
Ayan?" Rayan looked at him. "She's alive." Adam felt a wave of
relief. "Where?" "I don't know." "You just said she's alive." "I
know." "Then where is she?" Rayan swallowed. "They took her."
"Who?" Rayan looked toward the window. "The same people who
killed your father." Adam froze. "My father wasn't murdered."
Rayan's eyes met his. "That's what they wanted everyone to
believe." Rayan reached into his pocket and pulled out a small
flash drive. He placed it in Adam's hand. "Everything." Adam
stared at it. "What's on this?" "The names." "Whose names?"
Rayan looked toward the window. "The people who ordered your
father's death." Adam's fingers tightened around the drive. "And
Ayan?" Rayan's expression changed. "She found the same
information." "How?" "She was looking for her uncle." Adam's
eyes widened. "Her uncle?" Rayan nodded. "He disappeared the
same night your father died." Suddenly, headlights appeared
outside. The black Toyota. Rayan looked at Adam. "They found
us." A gunshot shattered the window. Adam dropped to the floor.
Rayan grabbed him. "Run!" Another shot. Glass exploded across
the room. Adam clutched the flash drive. And as they ran toward
the back door, his phone vibrated. One message. From Ayan.
Ayan: Adam, if Rayan tells you he loves me, don't believe him.
Adam stopped. He looked at Rayan. Rayan looked back. For the
first time, Adam noticed something he had never noticed before.
Rayan wasn't surprised. He was afraid. And that was when Adam
realized— Rayan wasn't hiding the truth from him. He was hiding
who he really was.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.text:
They ran through the back door. Adam didn't know where he
was going. He only knew he had to keep moving. Behind them,
another gunshot cracked through the night. Rayan grabbed
Adam's shoulder. "Left!" They disappeared into a narrow alley.
Adam's breathing was heavy. His hand was still wrapped around
the flash drive. "Stop." Rayan kept walking. "Rayan!" He finally
turned. Adam held up his phone. Ayan's message was still on the
screen. Ayan: If Rayan tells you he loves me, don't believe him.
Adam stared at him. "What does that mean?" Rayan said nothing.
"Why would she say that?" "I don't know." "You're lying." "I'm
trying to keep you alive." "Then start telling me the truth." Rayan
looked around the alley. "We don't have time." "Make time."
Rayan's eyes hardened. "You want the truth?" "Yes." "You've been
looking at the wrong person." Adam frowned. "What?" "You're
asking why Ayan disappeared." "Yes." "You should be asking why
she found you." Adam went silent. Rayan stepped closer. "Ayan
didn't meet you by accident." Adam shook his head. "That's not
possible." "It is." "She told me she remembered seeing me at the
training." "She did." "Then what's the problem?" "The problem
is..." Rayan paused. "...she had already seen your name before
she ever saw your face." Adam felt something sink inside him.
"Where?" Rayan looked at the flash drive. "On your father's
documents." They reached an abandoned shop at the end of the
alley. Rayan forced open the back door. Inside was darkness and
dust. They sat on the floor. Adam placed the flash drive between
them. "What's on it?" Rayan pulled out a laptop. "Your father
spent years collecting evidence." "Against who?" "People with
money. Influence. Connections." Adam stared at him. "And you
knew?" "I knew pieces." "Why didn't you tell me?" "Because
knowing the truth got people killed." Rayan plugged in the drive.
A folder appeared. PROJECT NIGHTFALL Adam stared at the
name. He clicked it. There were dozens of files. Documents.
Photographs. Bank records. Names. Then one photograph
opened. Adam's heart stopped. It was Ayan. But she looked much
younger. Maybe seventeen. She was standing beside an older
man. Adam recognized him immediately. Her uncle. Rayan
pointed at the screen. "That's where everything started." Adam
zoomed in. Behind Ayan was a building. A small blue building.

The same building from the photograph she had sent him months
ago. Adam looked at Rayan. "She knew." "Yes." "She knew about
my father." "Yes." "Then why didn't she tell me?" Rayan looked
away. "Because she was afraid." "Of what?" "Of what would
happen if you found out who your father really was." Adam stared
at the screen. "Who was he?" Rayan took a breath. "He wasn't
just investigating them." Adam looked at him. "He was one of
them." Silence. Adam slowly shook his head. "No." "Your father
was part of the organization before he turned against them."
Adam stood. "You're lying." "I'm not." "My father was a good
man." "I know." "Then why would he—" "Because he discovered
what they were doing." Rayan looked at him. "And when he tried
to leave, they killed him." Adam couldn't speak. His whole
childhood suddenly felt like a lie. The man he remembered as his
hero had lived another life. A hidden life. A dangerous one. Then
another file opened automatically. A list of names. At the bottom
was one name highlighted in red. RAYAN HASSAN. Adam looked
at him. "What is this?" Rayan didn't answer. "Your name is here."
"I know." "Why?" Rayan looked down. "Because my father was
the one who recruited yours." Adam's face changed. "You knew
everything." "Not everything." "You knew enough." Rayan's voice
softened. "I was trying to protect you." Adam laughed bitterly.
"You've been lying to me for years." "I was trying to keep you
alive." "And Ayan?" Rayan looked at the screen. "I loved her
before you did." Adam froze. The words hung between them.
"You..." Rayan swallowed. "Yes." "When?" "Before you ever met
her." Adam stared at him. "Does she love you?" Rayan looked
away. "She did." Adam's chest tightened. "And now?" "I don't
know." For a moment, Adam couldn't tell which hurt more. The
lies. The betrayal. Or the possibility that the woman he loved had
once loved his best friend. Then Rayan said something that
changed everything. "But that's not why she chose you." Adam
looked at him. "Then why?" Rayan reached into his pocket. He
pulled out an old photograph. He placed it on the table. It showed
three men standing outside a building. His father. Rayan's father.
And another man. For a moment, Adam noticed something
strange in the photograph: Rayan was standing beside another
young man who looked almost exactly like him. Adam glanced at
Rayan. Rayan quietly took the photograph back and slid it
beneath the others. Adam assumed the boy was a cousin and
thought nothing more of it. The third man's face had been
scratched out. But someone had written a name beneath him.
HASSAN ADAN. Adam's blood ran cold. "That's my grandfather."
Rayan nodded. "Exactly." Adam looked at the photograph again.

His grandfather had died before he was born. As far as he knew,
he had never been involved in anything dangerous. Rayan spoke
quietly. "Your family has been connected to this since before you
were born." Adam turned the photograph over. There was a
handwritten message on the back. When the boy turns
twenty-five, give him the truth. Adam stared at the sentence.
"Who wrote this?" Rayan didn't answer. Adam looked up. "Who?"
Rayan's expression changed. "Ayan." Adam's heart stopped. "She
found this years ago." "When?" "Before she met you." Adam
looked at the photograph again. Ayan had known. She had known
about his family. She had known about his father. She had known
about the people watching him. And still... she had fallen in love
with him. Or had she? Adam's phone suddenly vibrated. A video.
He opened it. The screen showed a dark room. Ayan was sitting
on a chair. Her hands were tied. There was a bruise on her cheek.
Adam's breath caught. "Ayan..." She looked directly into the
camera. She seemed exhausted. But alive. A man's voice came
from behind the camera. "Adam." Adam froze. "Your father made
a mistake." The man stepped into the frame. His face remained
hidden. "He thought he could destroy us." The camera moved
closer to Ayan. "But he left behind something much more
valuable." Adam's heart pounded. "What?" The man laughed
softly. "His son." The video ended. Adam looked at Rayan.
Neither of them spoke. Then Rayan whispered: "They don't want
the flash drive." Adam looked at him. "They want you." Outside, a
car engine started. Then another. Rayan closed the laptop. "We
need to move." Adam stood. But before he could take a step, his
phone vibrated again. This time, there was no message. Only a
photograph. Adam opened it. His blood ran cold. It was a
photograph of him and Ayan from their very first day together.
But someone had written across the image in black ink: SHE WAS
NEVER SUPPOSED TO FALL IN LOVE WITH YOU. Adam stared
at the words. And suddenly, he understood the most frightening
part. Ayan hadn't been taken because she knew the secret. She
had been taken because... she had chosen him.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching
chapters.text:
The city looked different after midnight. Nairobi was still
awake, but Adam felt as though he were moving through a place
that no longer belonged to him. Every car seemed suspicious.
Every shadow looked like a person. Every phone vibration made
his heart jump. Rayan drove without speaking. Adam sat beside
him, staring through the window. Ayan's face remained in his
mind. The photograph. The bruise. Her frightened eyes. He
couldn't stop thinking about one thing. She had chosen him. But
why? "Where are we going?" Adam finally asked. "Somewhere
they won't find us." "That's what you said before." Rayan glanced
at him. "You don't trust me." "Should I?" Rayan didn't answer.
Adam looked down at his phone. The video was still there. He
played it again. Ayan appeared on the screen. She looked tired.
Scared. But when she looked into the camera, Adam noticed
something. Her eyes moved slightly to the left. Then back. Then
left again. Adam paused the video. "Wait." Rayan looked at him.
"What's wrong?" "Play it." Rayan did. Adam watched carefully.
Ayan moved her eyes again. Left. Then down. Adam's mind raced.
"She's trying to tell us something." "What?" "I don't know yet." He
replayed the video. This time he watched the background. A small
table. A metal door. A clock. And something hanging on the wall.
A photograph. Adam zoomed in. The image was blurry. But he
could make out a familiar place. "The blue building." Rayan's eyes
widened. "You're sure?" "That's where she was." Rayan
immediately turned the car around. "Where are you going?" "The
old warehouse." "What warehouse?" "The building behind the
photograph." Adam stared at him. "You know it?" Rayan nodded.
"My father used it." "For what?" "Meetings." Adam's stomach
tightened. "Then that's where they're keeping her." "Maybe."
"Then let's go." Rayan didn't argue. The warehouse stood at the
edge of an industrial area. Dark. Abandoned. Silent. Rayan
parked several streets away. They approached on foot. Adam's
heart was pounding. "Stay behind me," Rayan whispered. They
reached the side entrance. Unlocked. Rayan looked at Adam.
"Too easy." They stepped inside. The building smelled of dust and
oil. Their footsteps echoed. Then they heard something. A faint
sound. Metal scraping against the floor. Adam turned. "Ayan?"
No answer. They moved deeper inside. Then the lights came on.

Adam froze. A voice came through a speaker. "Welcome." Rayan
pulled Adam backward. A door slammed behind them. Locked.
The voice continued. "You came faster than expected." Adam
looked around. "Where is she?" A screen on the wall switched on.
Ayan appeared. This time, she wasn't tied to a chair. She was
standing. And someone was standing behind her. A man in a
black jacket. His face was still hidden. Adam stepped forward.
"Let her go." The man laughed. "You still think you're in control."
Adam clenched his fists. "What do you want?" "Your father's final
file." Rayan spoke. "It's gone." "No." The man's voice became
colder. "It's with you." Adam looked at the flash drive. The man
continued. "You don't even know what you have." "Then tell me."
"Not yet." Ayan suddenly shouted: "Adam, don't listen to him!"
The man grabbed her arm. Adam moved forward. "Don't touch
her." The man smiled. "Interesting." He looked at Ayan. "He's
exactly like his father." Ayan's expression changed. "Adam..." The
screen went black. Then the warehouse lights shut off. A gunshot
exploded in the darkness. Rayan grabbed Adam. "Move!" They
ran. Another shot. Then another. Adam felt something hit his
shoulder. He stumbled. "Adam!" "I'm okay." Rayan dragged him
through a side door. They ran into the night. Only when they
reached the car did they stop. Adam looked at his shoulder.
Blood. A bullet had grazed him. Rayan tore part of his shirt and
wrapped the wound. "You could have died." "So could Ayan."
Rayan looked at him. "You're willing to die for her." Adam stared
into the darkness. "Yes." Rayan nodded slowly. "I know." They got
into the car. But before Rayan started the engine, Adam noticed
something. A small piece of paper had been placed beneath the
windshield wiper. He took it. Three words were written on it.
LOOK BEHIND YOU. Adam slowly turned. Across the road stood
a woman. Wearing a red scarf. Adam's heart stopped. "Ayan?"
The woman looked at him. Then stepped into the light. It wasn't
Ayan. She smiled. And walked away. Rayan stared after her.
"Who was that?" Adam didn't answer. Because he recognized her.
She was one of the women who had been standing beside Ayan
the first day they met. The woman who had introduced them. The
woman Adam had completely forgotten about. His phone
vibrated. A message appeared. Unknown: Now you understand.
Then another. Unknown: She was never the beginning. Adam
stared at the screen. A final message appeared. Unknown: She
was the bait.

chapters.title: The Secret She Kept
chapters.text:
Ayan woke to the sound of rain. For a few seconds, she didn't
remember where she was. Then she felt the cold metal around
her wrists. The room came back to her. The chair. The bare walls.
The single light above her. She looked around. Nobody was there.
She closed her eyes. Adam. She pictured his face. His smile. The
way he looked at her whenever she spoke. The way he always
told her she didn't have to pretend around him. A tear rolled
down her cheek. She had wanted to tell him everything. From the
beginning. But fear had always been louder than courage. A door
opened. A man walked inside. This time, Ayan saw his face. She
immediately recognized him. "You." He smiled. "Hello, Ayan." She
looked away. "You shouldn't have come back." "I didn't have a
choice." "Everyone has a choice." She laughed bitterly. "Not
when you have people you love." The man's smile disappeared.
"That's exactly why you're here." He placed a folder on the table.
"Adam." Ayan's eyes moved toward it. "Leave him alone." "You
brought him into this." "No." "You fell in love with him." Ayan said
nothing. The man opened the folder. Inside were photographs.
Adam. Walking. Talking. Sleeping in his car. Leaving his house.
Meeting Ayan. Everything. Ayan's face went pale. "How long?"
"We've been watching him for months." "Why?" "Because of his
father." Ayan shook her head. "His father is dead." "His secrets
aren't." The man closed the folder. "Where is the flash drive?" "I
don't know." "You do." "I don't." He leaned closer. "Then perhaps
we should talk about Adam." Ayan's voice became cold. "Don't
touch him." The man smiled. "There it is." "What?" "That's the
problem." He stood. "You were supposed to get close to him."
Ayan looked at him. "You were supposed to gain his trust." "I
know." "You were supposed to find the file." "I know." "And then
disappear." Ayan's eyes filled with tears. "But you fell in love with
him." She looked away. "I didn't mean to." The man laughed.
"Nobody ever does." Two months earlier, Ayan sat across from
the same woman who had later stood outside the warehouse. Her
name was Leila. She had been Ayan's closest friend for years.
"Are you sure about this?" Leila asked. Ayan nodded. "I have to
find the truth." "And Adam?" Ayan looked away. "He's part of the
plan." "Do you know who he is?" "Yes." "Do you know who his
father was?" "Yes." Leila lowered her voice. "Then you know what

happens if they find out you're getting attached." Ayan nodded. "I
won't." Leila looked at her. "You already are." Ayan smiled sadly.
"I can control it." "You can't." Ayan looked through the window.
Across the street, Adam was standing outside the training hall.
He was laughing with someone. She watched him. Then
whispered: "He's different." Leila sighed. "That's what scares
me." Ayan had never planned to love him. She had planned to use
him. That was the truth she could never bring herself to tell
Adam. The first time she saw him, she already knew his name.
She knew where he lived. She knew about his father. She knew
about the old investigation. She knew that one day Adam would
eventually find the truth. Her job was simple. Get close. Gain his
trust. Find the missing file. Disappear. But Adam had ruined the
plan by becoming real. He wasn't the arrogant, careless man she
expected. He listened. He remembered small things. He noticed
when she was sad. He never forced her to speak. And when she
told him about her fears, he didn't laugh. He simply said: "You
don't have to be afraid with me." That sentence destroyed
everything. Because she believed him. Back in the room, Ayan
looked at the man. "Where is Rayan?" "Why?" "Because if you're
watching Adam, you know he isn't working alone." The man
smiled. "Rayan has always been part of this." Ayan's eyes
hardened. "You're lying." "Am I?" He placed another photograph
on the table. Rayan was standing beside a man. His father. And
beside them... Ayan's uncle. Ayan stared at the picture. Her
breathing stopped. Her uncle had been missing for nine years.
She had spent years believing he was dead. But in the
photograph, he was alive. And smiling. Ayan whispered: "Where
did you get this?" The man said nothing. Then he turned the
photograph over. There was a date. Three weeks ago. Ayan's
hands began shaking. "No..." The man smiled. "Your uncle is
alive." Ayan looked up. "Where?" "That's what you need to find
out." Meanwhile, Adam sat in the passenger seat while Rayan
drove. Neither had spoken for several minutes. Finally Adam
asked: "Who was that woman?" "Leila." "She's Ayan's friend."
"Yes." "Why was she there?" "I don't know." Adam looked at him.
"You're lying again." Rayan sighed. "Leila was the person who
introduced Ayan to you." Adam stared ahead. "I know." "But she
wasn't supposed to." "What do you mean?" Rayan's hands
tightened around the steering wheel. "Ayan was supposed to
meet you somewhere else." "Why?" "Because someone wanted
her to meet you." Adam's face hardened. "Who?" Rayan didn't
answer. "Who, Rayan?" Finally, Rayan said: "My father." Adam
looked at him. "What?" "My father arranged the meeting." The

car became silent. Adam slowly shook his head. "So all of this..."
"Yes." "The training." "The bus." "Everything?" Rayan nodded.
"Everything." Adam felt sick. He thought about the first time he
saw Ayan. The red scarf. Her smile. The long conversations. The
first time she looked at him. Was any of it real? Then his phone
vibrated. A message. From Ayan. Adam opened it. There was only
one sentence. Ayan: Adam, I am sorry I lied to you. But I never
lied about loving you. He stared at the screen. For the first time
since Ayan disappeared, he smiled. A small, broken smile.
Because even in the middle of all the lies... there was one thing
he still wanted to believe. Her love was real. Then another
message arrived. Ayan: Don't come looking for me. Adam's smile
disappeared. A second message followed. Ayan: Because if you
find me, they will kill you. And then the final message. Ayan: But
if you still choose to come... come alone. Adam looked at Rayan.
Rayan already knew. "You're going after her." Adam nodded.
"Yes." Rayan sighed. "Then I'm coming with you." Adam shook his
head. "No." Rayan looked at him. "Why?" Adam looked down at
Ayan's message. "Because she asked me to come alone." For the
first time, Rayan looked genuinely afraid. "Adam..." Adam opened
the car door. "Stay here." He stepped out. Rayan watched him
disappear into the darkness. Then his phone rang. He answered.
A man's voice whispered: "He's going to her." Rayan closed his
eyes. "I know." "Then you know what happens next." Rayan
looked toward the road. "No." He paused. "I'm not letting you kill
him." The call ended. Rayan stared at the darkness. Because he
knew something Adam didn't. Ayan hadn't asked Adam to come
alone because she wanted to protect him. She had asked him to
come alone because... she was planning to betray everyone.

chapters.title: The Man Behind The Door
chapters.text:
Adam walked alone. The rain had stopped, but the streets were
still wet. Ayan's last message remained on his screen. Come
alone. He had no idea where he was going. Only one clue. A
location. An old address Ayan had sent him once, months ago,
when they were talking about childhood memories. He had never
asked why. Now he understood. The address led him to an
abandoned house on the outskirts of the city. The gate was open.
Adam stopped outside. Every instinct told him to turn around. He
didn't. He stepped inside. The house was dark. The front door
was slightly open. "Ayan?" Nothing. He entered. The door closed
behind him. Adam turned quickly. Locked. Then a light came on.
Ayan was sitting at a table. Her hands were free. There was no
blood on her. No rope. No visible injury. Adam stared at her. For
a moment, neither spoke. Then he whispered: "You're okay." Ayan
looked at him. "I'm sorry." Adam walked toward her. "I thought
you were hurt." "I was." "What happened?" She looked down. "I
had to make them believe I was afraid." Adam stopped. "You
weren't kidnapped?" "I was." "But you escaped?" "No." Adam
frowned. "Then how are you here?" Ayan looked toward the
hallway. "Because they wanted me here." Adam's expression
changed. "What?" "They knew you'd come." Ayan stood. "They've
been watching you since the beginning." Adam's voice became
cold. "Who are they?" Ayan hesitated. "People connected to your
father." "I already know that." "No." She shook her head. "Your
father was kept alive in secret." Ayan walked toward a locked
door at the end of the hallway. She pulled out a key. Adam
watched. "What is behind that door?" "The reason your father
died." The key turned. The door opened. Inside was a small room
filled with boxes. Photographs. Old newspapers. Documents. And
dozens of photographs of Adam. From different ages. Adam
stared. "How long have they been watching me?" "Since you were
born." His stomach dropped. "Why?" Ayan picked up an old
photograph. It showed Adam as a child. Standing beside his
father. "He wasn't protecting you from them." Adam looked at
her. "He was protecting them from you." "What does that mean?"
Ayan turned the photograph over. There was a handwritten
message. THE BOY MUST NEVER KNOW. Adam's voice
trembled. "Know what?" Ayan looked into his eyes. "Your father

didn't die because he betrayed them." She paused. "He died
because he stole something from them." "What?" "The original
evidence." Adam looked around the room. "Where is it?" Ayan
shook her head. "I don't know." "Then why bring me here?"
"Because you have it." Adam frowned. "No, I don't." Ayan stepped
closer. "You do." She pointed toward the photograph in his hand.
"Look at your father's watch." Adam examined the photograph.
His father was wearing an old silver watch. Adam suddenly
remembered. His father had given him that watch when he was
sixteen. He still had it. Ayan whispered: "Open it." Adam stared at
her. "My watch?" "Yes." "Why?" "Because your father knew one
day they would come for you." Adam immediately took out his
phone. "I left it at home." Ayan's face changed. "Then we have to
go." A sound came from the hallway. Both froze. Footsteps.
Someone was walking toward them. Ayan whispered: "They found
us." Adam looked at the door. "How?" Ayan shook her head. "I
don't know." The footsteps stopped outside. Then came three
knocks. Adam's blood went cold. The same three knocks. Ayan
looked at him. "You know that sound." Adam nodded. "Yes." The
door opened. A man stepped inside. Adam recognized him.
Rayan's father. The same man from the photograph. The man
Adam had believed was simply an old family friend. He smiled.
"Hello, Adam." Adam stepped in front of Ayan. "You killed my
father." The man's expression didn't change. "Your father made a
mistake." "What did he steal?" "The truth." Adam clenched his
fists. "Where is my father?" "That is what the world was told." "I
know that." "No." The man smiled. "Your father was kept alive in
secret." Adam froze. The man looked at Ayan. "Tell him." Ayan
shook her head. The man continued. "Tell him what you saw."
Adam looked at Ayan. "What is he talking about?" Ayan's eyes
filled with tears. "I saw your father after he was supposed to be
dead." Adam stared at her. "What?" "Nine years ago." Ayan's
voice trembled. "I saw him." Adam couldn't breathe. "Where?"
"Garissa." The room became silent. "He wasn't killed that night,"
Ayan continued. "He was taken." Adam shook his head. "Taken by
who?" Rayan's father answered. "By me." Adam lunged toward
him. Ayan grabbed his arm. "Adam, no!" The man smiled. "Your
father was alive for six months after the world believed he was
dead." Adam's eyes filled with disbelief. "Why?" "Because he
refused to tell us where he hid the evidence." "Where is he now?"
The man looked at him. "Still alive. But hidden." Adam's voice
cracked. "Then why did everyone think he was dead?" The man
didn't answer. Instead, he said: "Ask Rayan. He knows what
happened next." Adam froze. Ayan closed her eyes. Adam slowly

turned toward her. "What does Rayan have to do with my father's
death?" Ayan whispered: "He was there." Adam stepped back.
"No." "He was there that night." "No." "He saw everything."
Adam shook his head. "Rayan was my friend." Ayan looked at him.
"I know." Then the lights went out. A gunshot exploded. The man
fell. Ayan screamed. Adam grabbed her. "Run!" They rushed
toward the back door. But before they could escape, a voice came
from the darkness. "Adam." He stopped. He knew that voice.
Rayan. The lights flickered back on. Rayan stood at the doorway.
His gun was raised. Ayan looked at him. "Rayan..." He stared at
Adam. "I'm sorry." Adam's heart sank. Rayan lowered the gun.
Then he said something Adam would never forget. "I didn't kill
your father." A pause. "I was the one who tried to save him."
Behind Rayan, another figure appeared. The man Adam thought
had been shot... was standing. Alive. He smiled. And Adam finally
understood. The entire confrontation had been a setup. Ayan
hadn't betrayed him. Rayan hadn't betrayed him. They had all
been playing the same dangerous game. But there was still one
question. Who was the man they were really trying to protect
Adam from? Then Rayan looked at Adam and whispered: "Your
father." Adam's face went pale. "What?" Rayan looked toward the
man behind him. "He is alive. Your father was never killed when
they said he was. His death was staged, and he has been hiding
ever since."

chapters.title: Love Was The Bait
chapters.text:
Adam couldn't move. His father's name seemed to echo
through the room. He's alive. Nine years. Nine years of believing
he was dead. Nine years of visiting a grave. Nine years of
carrying memories of a man who, apparently, had never been
buried there. Adam looked at Rayan. "Say it again." Rayan
swallowed. "Your father is alive." Adam shook his head. "That's
impossible." The older man stepped forward. "You were always
told I was dead." Adam looked at him. The man's face was partly
hidden by the darkness. Then he stepped into the light. Adam
stopped breathing. The face was older. Thinner. Marked by years
of pain. But the eyes— Adam knew those eyes. His knees almost
gave way. "Dad?" The man looked at him. For the first time, the
cold expression disappeared. "Adam." Adam stepped backward.
"No." His voice broke. "You can't be here." His father looked
down. "I know." "You let me believe you were dead." "I had no
choice." "You had no choice?" Adam's anger finally exploded. "I
cried at your grave!" His father closed his eyes. "I know." "You
watched me grow up without you!" "I know." "You watched me
suffer!" "I know." Adam pushed him. "Then why?" His father
didn't fight back. "Because if they knew you were my son, they
would have killed you." Adam stepped away. "Who are they?" His
father looked toward Rayan. Rayan nodded. "Tell him." Adam's
father took a slow breath. "They aren't an organization." Adam
frowned. "They are people." "Who?" "Politicians. Businessmen.
Officials. People who built their lives by stealing from others." He
looked at Ayan. "Her uncle discovered them." Ayan lowered her
eyes. "My uncle tried to expose them." Adam's father nodded.
"Your father helped him." Adam looked at Ayan. "Then what
happened?" "They found out." His father continued. "They killed
Ayan's uncle." Ayan's eyes filled with tears. "No." Her father
shook his head. "That's what they wanted everyone to believe."
Ayan looked at him. "What do you mean?" "Your uncle escaped."
Adam stared. "He's alive?" His father nodded. "He has been
hiding for years." Ayan covered her mouth. "Where?" "Safe."
"Where?" "I can't tell you." Ayan stepped toward him. "He's my
family." "And that's exactly why they can use him against you."
Silence. Adam looked at his father. "Then why was Ayan brought
into this?" His father didn't answer immediately. Ayan did.

"Because I knew where the evidence was." Adam looked at her.
"Did you?" "No." She shook her head. "But they thought I did."
Adam remembered the first message. If anything happens to me,
don't trust the person who tells you I left. He finally understood.
She had known they were coming. She had been trying to warn
him. His father looked at him. "Your mother kept something from
you." "What?" "Your father's watch." Adam's eyes widened. "I
have it." "Where?" "At home." His father looked at Rayan. "Go."
Rayan nodded. But before he could leave, Ayan stopped him.
"Wait." Everyone looked at her. She reached into her pocket. "I
have something." She pulled out a small photograph. Adam took
it. It was a photograph of his father standing with a young Ayan.
On the back was a message. Protect Adam. Even if he hates you
for it. Adam looked at Ayan. "You knew my father?" "Yes." "Before
we met?" "Yes." "How long?" "Since I was seventeen." Adam
stared at her. "Then our relationship..." Ayan's eyes filled with
tears. "At first, it was part of the plan." Adam's heart broke. Ayan
continued. "I was supposed to get close to you." "To find the
evidence." "Yes." He looked away. "So everything was a lie."
"No." She stepped toward him. "The beginning was a lie." Adam
looked at her. "But not the ending." Ayan's voice trembled. "I
didn't expect to love you." Adam said nothing. "I tried to leave
you." She wiped her tears. "More than once." "Then why didn't
you?" "Because every time I looked at you, I forgot why I came."
Adam's eyes softened. For the first time, his anger began to
crack. His father watched them silently. Then he said: "Love was
never supposed to be part of the plan." Ayan looked at Adam.
"But it became the most dangerous part." Suddenly, a loud crash
came from outside. Rayan ran to the window. "Cars." His face
changed. "Three." Adam's father stood. "They found us." Ayan
grabbed Adam's hand. "Come." They ran toward the back exit.
But before they reached it, the lights went out. A gunshot. Then
another. Rayan shouted: "DOWN!" Everyone dropped. Another
shot. Then another. Adam's father pulled a gun. Ayan grabbed
Adam's hand. "Stay with me." They ran through the back door.
Rain poured down. They reached a waiting car. Rayan opened the
driver's door. "Get in!" Adam pushed Ayan inside. Then he heard
a voice behind him. "Adam!" He turned. A man stood across the
road. The same man who had been sending the messages. He
removed his hood. Adam recognized him. His blood ran cold. It
was someone he had trusted for years. Someone who had been
beside him during every difficult moment. Someone who knew
everything. Adam whispered: "Rayan?" But Rayan was already
sitting beside him in the car. Adam turned. The man across the

road smiled. He wasn't Rayan. He was Rayan's twin brother—the
boy from the photograph Adam had noticed earlier, but never
knew the truth about. The man raised his phone. One final
message appeared on Adam's screen. You found the truth. Then
another. But you still haven't found the traitor. The car sped
away. Adam looked at Ayan. She was holding his hand tightly.
Neither spoke. Because they both knew. The danger wasn't
behind them anymore. It was already inside their circle.

chapters.title: The Last Message
chapters.text:
The car disappeared into the darkness. Nobody spoke. Rayan
drove faster than Adam had ever seen him drive. Ayan sat beside
Adam in the back seat. Her hand was still holding his. Neither of
them wanted to let go. Finally, Adam looked at her. "Tell me
everything." Ayan looked down. "I will." "No more secrets." "I
promise." "Even if it hurts?" She looked into his eyes. "Especially
if it hurts." Adam nodded. "Then start with the first day." Ayan
took a deep breath. "The first day I saw you wasn't the first day I
knew about you." Adam listened. "I knew your name before I
knew your face." "Because of my father?" "Yes." She paused. "My
uncle left me a photograph and a message. He told me that if
anything happened to him, I had to find your father." "Why?"
"Because your father was the only person he trusted." Adam
looked away. "And then?" "I found your name." "How?" "Through
the old files." She squeezed his hand. "I was supposed to get
close to you." Adam's chest tightened. "I know." "I was supposed
to find the evidence your father had hidden." "And you couldn't."
"I found something else." "What?" Ayan looked at him. "You."
Adam didn't speak. "I started falling for you before I realized it."
She smiled sadly. "You remember the first time you asked me
why I was quiet?" "Yes." "I went quiet because I knew I was
already lying to you." Adam lowered his eyes. "And the night you
told me you loved me?" "I meant it." "Even though you were using
me?" "I stopped using you long before that." Adam looked at her.
"Then why didn't you tell me?" "Because by then, telling you the
truth could have killed you." Silence filled the car. Then Adam
said: "I forgive you." Ayan looked at him. "You do?" "Not
everything." She smiled through her tears. "But enough." She
rested her head against his shoulder. For the first time in days,
Adam felt something close to peace. Then Rayan spoke from the
front. "We have a problem." Adam looked up. "What?" "We can't
go home." "Why?" Rayan pointed toward the rear-view mirror. A
black car was following them. Then another appeared behind it.
Ayan sat upright. "They found us." Rayan accelerated. The cars
followed. Adam looked at his father. "Where are we going?" His
father looked through the window. "Somewhere they won't
expect." "Where?" "Garissa." Adam stared. "Back to where this
started?" His father nodded. "That's where the final piece is."

Three hours later, they arrived. The town was quiet. Adam
stepped out of the car. Everything felt strangely familiar. The
road. The air. The darkness. He remembered the bus journey
with Ayan. Her red scarf. Her earphones. The way she had looked
out the window. Ayan stood beside him. "I remember this place."
Adam looked at her. "So do I." His father walked ahead. "We
don't have much time." They followed him to an old house. The
door opened with a rusty sound. Inside was a small room. A table.
Two chairs. And a safe built into the wall. Adam's father removed
a key from his pocket. He opened it. Inside was a single envelope.
Adam stared at it. "That's it?" His father nodded. "The original
evidence." Adam took the envelope. His hands trembled. He
opened it. Inside were photographs. Bank transfers. Names.
Dates. Then one document made him stop. It was a death
certificate. His father's name was on it. But the date was wrong.
Adam looked up. "You were declared dead six months before you
actually died." His father nodded. "Because they needed everyone
to believe it." Adam looked at the papers. Then he found
something else. A list of names. At the bottom was a handwritten
note: The person who leaked our operation is inside the family.
Adam looked at Rayan. Rayan looked confused. His father read
the note. Then his face changed. "What?" Adam asked. His father
didn't answer. "Who is it?" His father turned the page. There was
a photograph attached. Adam stared at it. His heart stopped. The
person in the photograph was... Ayan. Adam looked at her.
"Ayan?" She stepped closer. "I've never seen that." His father
shook his head. "Then someone has framed you." Suddenly— A
gunshot shattered the window. The lights went out. Everyone
dropped. Another shot. Then another. Rayan shouted: "Back
door!" Adam grabbed Ayan. They ran. But his father didn't move.
"Dad!" "Go!" Adam stopped. "No!" His father looked at him. "You
have to leave." Another gunshot. His father fell. "DAD!" Adam
rushed back. Blood spread across his father's shirt. Ayan grabbed
Adam. "He's still alive!" Rayan pulled them toward the door. "We
have to go!" Adam looked back. His father was lying on the floor.
Still breathing. Still looking at him. And with the last strength in
his voice, he whispered: "Don't trust..." He coughed. Adam leaned
closer. "Don't trust who?" His father looked past him. Toward
Rayan. Then whispered: "...the one you love most." Adam froze.
Ayan heard it too. She looked at him. Adam looked at her. Neither
spoke. Outside, sirens began approaching. Rayan pulled Adam
away. "Move!" They escaped into the darkness. An hour later,
Adam sat alone in an abandoned room. Ayan was outside with
Rayan. Adam couldn't stop thinking about his father's final words.

Don't trust the one you love most. He closed his eyes. Then his
phone vibrated. A message. From an unknown number. Adam
opened it. There was no text. Only an audio recording. He
pressed play. His father's voice filled the room. "If you're hearing
this, I'm probably dead." Adam's eyes filled with tears. "I need
you to know one thing." A pause. "Your mother wasn't the only
person I was protecting." Another pause. "I was protecting you
from someone you have known your entire life." Adam's
breathing stopped. Then his father said: "The person who
betrayed me..." A long silence. "...was never Rayan." The
recording ended. Adam stared at the screen. Outside the room,
he heard Ayan laughing softly with Rayan. His phone vibrated
again. One final message appeared. Now ask Ayan what
happened to her uncle. Adam slowly stood. For the first time
since they had reunited... he wasn't sure whether he could trust
the woman he loved.

END OF SEASON ONE
The story continues in Season Two.
